prompt: Many manufactured food and drink products contain high levels of sugar, which causes many health problems. Sugary products should be made more expensive to encourage people to consume less sugar. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many manufactured foods and drinks contain excessive amounts of sugar, which can contribute to serious health problems such as obesity and diabetes. It has therefore been suggested that sugary products should be made more expensive to reduce their consumption. I largely agree with this proposal, although higher prices should be combined with education and clearer information about sugar content.

Increasing the price of sugary products could discourage people from purchasing them regularly. If soft drinks, sweets and processed foods become more expensive, customers may choose healthier alternatives such as water, fruit or products containing less sugar. This could be particularly effective for parents who regularly buy food and drinks for their children. Higher prices may also encourage businesses to reduce the amount of sugar in their products. If companies can avoid additional costs by producing healthier goods, they will have a financial reason to introduce new recipes and compete with other manufacturers. Furthermore, money collected through a sugar tax could be used to support public health services or educational campaigns.

However, increasing prices alone may not be sufficient. Some people may continue buying sugary products because of their habits, even if they become more expensive. The policy could also have a greater financial effect on low-income families, especially when healthier alternatives are not affordable or widely available. For this reason, governments should require manufacturers to display clear information about sugar levels on packaging. Schools and public health organizations should also explain the long-term effects of excessive sugar consumption. In addition, the extra charge should be based on the amount of sugar a product contains rather than being applied equally to every product.

In conclusion, I agree that products containing high levels of sugar should be more expensive because this could influence customers’ choices and encourage manufacturers to produce healthier goods. Nevertheless, the policy will be more effective and fair if it is supported by education, clear food labels and affordable alternatives.
